colophon: Thus ends the Raghavendra Raksha Kavacha, the fifth chapter of the Sri Raghavendra Tantra, composed by Sri Krishnavadhuta Pandita.

lines.1: Now I shall tell the wondrous protective armor of the noble Raghavendra,
lines.2: clad in which a person becomes secure and victorious.
lines.3: I, the beloved son of the king of gurus, honored by his grace,
lines.4: named Krishnavadhuta, tell this armor, which brings about his presence.
lines.5: Its meter is declared to be trishtubh; its deity, the king of gurus;
lines.6: the placing of the mantra should be done; I shall tell the meditation on the true guru.
lines.7: Holding a staff in his hand, bearing a rosary, eyes half open, seated on a lotus,
lines.8: lips gently moving, the guru who grants boons, fearlessness, and the wishes of those who bow: I remember him.
lines.9: Om. In the east, here, may Raghavendra protect me;
lines.10: in the south, may the destroyer of heavy sins guard me;
lines.11: in the west, may the giver of fearlessness guard me;
lines.12: in the northern direction, may the bringer of peace protect me.
lines.13: In the southeast, may the one of divine radiance guard me; in the southwest, the destroyer of the wicked;
lines.14: in the northwest, may the one with a body like diamond guard me; in the northeast, the giver of success.
lines.15: May he who took refuge at Rama's feet protect my topknot;
lines.16: may he whose nature is cool as the moon protect my head;
lines.17: may the remover of ill fortune guard my forehead;
lines.18: the remover of worldly torment, my brows.
lines.19: May the one rich in lineage and character guard my beard;
lines.20: may the giver of sight guard my eyes;
lines.21: may the remover of deafness guard my ears;
lines.22: the remover of the harm of poison, my cheeks.
lines.23: May the remover of hardship guard my lips;
lines.24: may the maker of sound always guard my nose;
lines.25: may the giver of speech always protect my tongue;
lines.26: may the giver of food always protect my teeth.
lines.27: May the lord of ascetics always protect my chin;
lines.28: may the lord of those under vows always protect my face;
lines.29: may the foremost devotee of the Lion guard my throat;
lines.30: may the one garlanded with flowers guard my shoulders.
lines.31: May the giver of strength here guard my arms;
lines.32: may the hero of boon-giving guard my hands;
lines.33: may the chanter of mantras guard my fingers;
lines.34: may the cutter of dense doubts guard my chest.
lines.35: May this destroyer of disease guard my belly;
lines.36: may the remover of the fear of worldly existence guard my sides;
lines.37: may the helper protect my back;
lines.38: may the one clad in gold always guard my hips.
lines.39: May the destroyer of urinary disease guard my secret parts;
lines.40: may the swift one always guard my thighs;
lines.41: may the one under the vow of silence guard my knees;
lines.42: may the giver of speed guard my shins.
lines.43: May the one worthy of praise for his virtues guard my ankles;
lines.44: may the enemy of those who oppress others guard my feet;
lines.45: whatever part of me I have not named here,
lines.46: may the compassionate one guard all of it.
lines.47: My ancestors, wives, sons, and kin,
lines.48: my grandsons and the rest: may the one who loves his children guard them.
lines.50: buffaloes and lions, jackals and thieves,
lines.51: the vicious ones, worms, scorpions, and creatures born from eggs:
lines.52: may the staff of the king of gurus strike them down and guard me.
lines.53: May the dust of the guru's feet break apart the pishachas, asuras, yakshas, rakshasas,
lines.54: ghosts, seizing spirits, and the rest.
lines.55: From fire, water, mountains, lightning, kings, enemies,
lines.56: poison and the like, may the water from the guru's feet guard me;
lines.57: and destroying leprosy, fever, piles, consumption, and the chief diseases,
lines.58: may that sacred clay guard me.
lines.60: and courage: may the guru Raghavendra guard these for me;
lines.61: power to win over kings, enemies, women, and men,
lines.62: friendship and love, poetry and learning;
lines.63: favor in all things, the attainment of every aim:
lines.64: may the foremost of the perfected ones grant these to me;
lines.65: knowledge, good conduct, a generous spirit,
lines.66: mind, senses, and the rest: may the all-knowing one protect these.
lines.68: discernment and the rest: may my father guard these;
lines.69: fulfillment of my resolves, the fulfillment of my words,
lines.70: and victory everywhere: may the beloved one grant these.
lines.71: May the giver of boons guard me in front;
lines.72: may the giver of strength guard me behind;
lines.73: may the remover of torment guard me above;
lines.74: may the giver of a steady dwelling guard me below.
lines.75: By day, at dawn, at night, at dusk,
lines.76: and at midday, may the ever-watchful one guard me;
lines.77: in all my undertakings, at all times,
lines.78: may the guru whose presence I have invoked protect me.
lines.79: This armor of the noble Raghavendra is the supreme protector,
lines.80: recited three times a day, or twice, or once:
lines.81: it calms leprosy and other diseases, removes every affliction, is auspicious,
lines.82: grants poetry, scriptural learning, and knowledge, and victory in debate;
lines.83: in the Kali age it is like the Brahma-weapon, for protection from every fear.
lines.84: I bow to the king of gurus, of fierce austerity, who humbles the pride of every enemy,
lines.85: rich in wealth like the king of the gods, who loves devotion, the true guru,
lines.86: who has tied on the bracelet vowing to rescue his devotees, remover of evil obstructions,
lines.87: whose generous heart surpasses the heavenly cow, the heavenly jewel, and the heavenly tree: that lord who brings well-being.
